## Context

The composer the phone exists for: surface 1, built from its artboard as a screen of its own after a first attempt built it as a box inside the session view and had this milestone's own scope row rewritten to match. Multi-line, spell-checked, one draft, and a destination chosen after the writing rather than before it.

## Done means

The box is the screen and the destination row is beneath it: thought first, destination second.
The route row defaults to the last active session, ordered by what tmux reports as activity rather than by name.
The idea inbox is a route beside the sessions, and choosing it files a record under the destination's own prefix rather than typing into anything.
A destination that is no longer on offer is named as gone rather than quietly replaced by another.
A project name containing a hyphen is a session, not a routing identifier.
The composer is spell-checked, autocapitalised and autocorrected, and Enter inserts a newline while Send submits.
One draft, under one key shared with the session view's reply box, written as it is typed so a backgrounded phone cannot lose it, and the header says it is kept only when the browser actually kept it.
A send that could not go leaves the text in the box, and the page says why; a send that went leaves the box empty.
A post that will not say where it came from is refused, as on the socket.
Multi-line arrives in a session as one message rather than one prompt per line.
The form posts and works with the script blocked, and the surface is served whether or not sessions are.

## Verified against

Real tmux and the real CLI, plus tests. What is asserted rather than measured is labelled as such in MUS-D-0096 and in the source.

The clause no test proves: that a bracketed paste reaches an agent's composer as ONE message rather than one prompt per line. Measured by hand against Claude Code — four lines pasted into a live pane, one Enter, and the agent answered from all four, replying 'ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE' to a message whose first three lines were those words. Plain send-keys also placed all four lines in the composer, which is why the mechanism is argued from reliability rather than from a failure to work.

What the tests prove, and on which surface. The composer's own delivery — a form POST, not a socket — reaches a real session with its lines in order and its newlines intact: TestMultiLineFromTheComposeSurfaceReachesTheSession. An earlier version of this record credited that to 'the composer over a real WebSocket'; the composer has no socket, and the test meant was the session view's reply box, which has its own real-tmux test. The composer's delivery was exercised by nothing until a review said so.

Also proven: Send uses the bracketed, self-cleaning paste path for multi-line and keystrokes for single-line. The destination row is ordered by activity and pre-selects the most recent, against a listing where the alphabetical answer and the correct one differ. A hyphenated project name is treated as a session. A vanished destination is named. The inbox files under IDW rather than the store's prefix, which caught that an explicitly chosen destination never read its prefix at all. A failed send returns the text and says why. A cross-origin post is refused. Exactly two surfaces carry script, asserted by a test that has the composer in its mux — the previous version did not, and passed while its name was false.

Neither real-tmux test discriminates between paste and keystrokes, because the panes hold cat and cat is happy with newlines either way. The session-package test says so in its comment; the web ones do not, and an earlier version of this record claimed both did.

## Risks

The done-when says from a phone, off the home network, without a terminal. The transport, the multi-line handling and the draft are verified here; the phone, the network and the browser's spell-checker are the owner's to confirm, as 2c's last sentence was.

A message can be started in three places — the composer, the session view's reply box, and the intake box. MUS-D-0013's fold clause asked for one; the owner declined the fold on MUS-Q-0036 and nothing is retired.

This is the second surface carrying script, taken on MUS-Q-0034 and bounded by the form working without it.

The paste buffer is named per process and per send. Nothing serialises two sends from the same process to the same session beyond that naming; they cannot collide, but their order is whatever tmux receives.

Enter-inserts-newline is a change in feel from the box that shipped at 4b, where Enter sent. Nobody has used either from a phone yet.

The draft is per-device, because the server holds no per-client state.
